notes.title: StarRupture Single-Player Playtest available now
notes.notes:
Featuring exciting single-player content, the StarRupture playtest will put you firmly into the treacherous world of Arcadia-7. Simply click the “[i]Request Access[/i]” button now on our Steam Page and enjoy it until July 31st.

While StarRupture is a co-op game at heart, where up to four players work together, we also want to ensure that the game is fun and engaging for those who play solo. 
This playtest will introduce you to the core elements of StarRupture, ranging from base building and exploration to survival and combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/39d1c56d37cd304499b73f115d1eea55e6338d55.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/6460036fe6da7948d75754d545b2dbcb612a41f8.png[/img]

[b]Welcome to StarRupture[/b], an intense first-person open-world survival game where you’ll build sprawling industrial bases, harvest valuable resources, and battle alien monsters. The planet is gorgeous, dangerous, and constantly evolving. Exploration, combat, and creativity are your keys to survival.

Meet Chris Bonnet - aka Prisoner 0212 - aka Scientist. He will be the character you play during the single-player playtest. You will have the opportunity to get to know him a little better during your time on Arcadia-7.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/7fc61da4a7cff71290591c7ced5e36b0e2007ab6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]🧪 Closed Playtest is available for a limited time only![/b][/h3]

The playtest kicks off J[b]uly 29 at 10:00 AM CEST / 1:00 AM PDT[/b] and ends [b]July 31 at 7:00 PM CEST / 10:00 AM PDT[/b]. To join, just head over to our Steam page and click “[i][b]Request Access[/b][/i]”. It’s that easy—and yes, it’s 100% free!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/0d6a4f8cad9d9bbf6a3b5d3469a49d0d0d1a71bf.gif[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1631270/StarRupture/

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]🎮 What’s in the Playtest?[/b][/h3]

The StarRupture Single-Player Playtest features over three hours of gameplay split between an early slice of the game featuring the game's core mechanics, a guided tutorial, and a free play option with map restrictions (the Playtest covers around 15% of the Early Access build map), but it’s a first taste of the fun that awaits in StarRupture. 

Some gameplay mechanics will be locked out for now (and left for you to fully explore when the game launches in Early Access this Autumn), such as wildlife, base attack and defense, corporate assignments and rewards over a certain level (6-7 depending on the corporation), the Forgotten Engine, some weapon unlocks with mods, and enemies. So don’t worry about the spoilers, the game will have plenty of fresh and new elements once it launches!

The Playtest supports English VO and interface localisation, and the full list of supported languages for StarRupture’s launch in Early Access is available on the game’s Steam Page.

There is no time limit on your session—play as much (or as little) as you want! However, [b]no co-op for now[/b]—we’re focusing on single-player balance and stability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/8d30579e3715ea9492082d22d8de1eae107d7951.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]🧱 Platforms & Requirements[/b][/h3]

[*] [b]Platform:[/b] PC via Steam
[*] [b]Controller Support:[/b] Not available yet
[*] [b]Ultrawide Support:[/b] Nope—for now
[*] [b]Download Size: [/b]~13 GB (~45 GB after installation)
[*] [b]Hardware Requirements - recommended:[/b] 
[list]
[*] Windows 10 or later, 64-bit 
[*] Intel Core i5 11400F / AMD Ryzen 5 5600 
[*] 24 GB RAM 
[*] NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 / AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT 
[*] DirectX 12 
[*] SSD Disk[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]🗣️ Languages & Access[/b][/h3]
[list][*] Playtest is English-only for now (interface + audio). You might find a few cases of AI voiceover; they are currently included in the build as placeholders and will be replaced by proper actor recordings for the Early Access release.
[*] No NDA! Share your experience publicly—screenshots, streams, memes, go wild. Maybe show off your wakiest base? Or the most impressive kill?
[*] Players will be selected randomly by Steam and will receive email notifications when they’re eligible to play. No Steam key required—access is added to your account.[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]💬 Feedback & Support[/b][/h3]

We want all kinds of feedback—from bug reports to general vibes and gameplay thoughts. Got a bug? Tell us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/starrupture]Discord[/url] or email support@creepyjar.com.

If you’d like to provide us with your feedback about the playtest, please fill out this short form:
https://forms.gle/WXi4ACxAakzCfozA6


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]❓Other Stuff You Should Know[/b][/h3]
[list][*] No criteria to sign up—just a PC and a Steam account
[*] If you’re not selected this round, you’re still in the pool for future tests
[*] There is no official age rating for the game yet, but we recommend 16+ (PEGI 16 / ESRB T guidelines)
[*] Want updates? Follow us on Steam and our socials
[*] Got questions? [url=https://discord.com/invite/starrupture]Join our Discord[/url]—our team and community are there to help
[*] More playtests? Stay tuned on our channels![/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[h3][b]🧠 The Big Goal[/b][/h3]

This test helps us with everything in the early game, including bug tracking, game balance, performance, feedback, and, most importantly, how the experience feels. You're helping shape StarRupture before its Early Access launch this Autumn. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/f8e6ead97f20ac7b59d0bbd2b9b2c31a817502ca.png[/img]

[b]PLAYTEST BUILD KNOWN ISSUES[/b]

Menu & Saves
[i][olist][*] Switching between tabs in the Options menu randomly causes some settings to become greyed out.
[*] The save file is not created in the slot selected by the player; it always saves to the first save slot on the left.[/olist][/i]
Gameplay
[i][olist][*] A crash may occur when attempting to place multiple Supported Platforms at once.
[*] A crash may occur when upgrading or deconstructing Rails.
[*] The game may temporarily freeze when placing multiple Supported Platforms for the first time in a session.
[*] Drones may stop delivering items to constructions. This can be resolved by deconstructing and rebuilding the affected rails and machines.
[*] When loading a save made during the Tutorial, the Tutorial widget does not appear until an objective is progressed.
[*] Dropped items stack up to a maximum of 100; any items beyond that limit disappear when dropped.
[*] If the Player obtains items with a full inventory, the excess items fall to the ground and may clip into each other.
[*] Deconstructing the entire base using the Deconstruction option in the Base Core spawns a container tower that may be unreachable by the Player.
[*] After reloading a session, all Quartz may disappear if the game was saved near a Quartz deposit. Quartz will reappear during the next Heat Wave.
[*] Unequipping the Building Tool while walking results in interrupting Player's movement.
[*] Hydration and Calories warning icons do not light up after loading a save.
[*] Machines set to OFF are turned back ON after reloading the save.
[*] The autosave function currently works only at the start and at the end of the tutorial.[/olist]
Visuals
[olist][*] The Map currently uses placeholder visuals.
[*] Enemies may occasionally appear slightly blurry or may flicker.
[*] Upon loading a save made during a Heat Wave, the critical temperature state and some visual effects may be missing.[/olist][/i]
Miscellaneous
[i][olist][*] Dialogues may overlap sporadically.[/olist][/i]

notes.title: StarRupture: Developer Update - June '25
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/75567d10c2e0e02a5deeeb4cb5eb512afd780085.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone!

Welcome to our fresh and exciting Developer Update. This month, we’re inviting you to check out our co-op mode in action, and we’re sharing more info about the effects of the scorching fire wave, and how you can unlock your inner interior designer.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img][/p][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/e1cb02b9a4215096823b3509391ef87d1e5a453c.png"][/img][/p][previewyoutube="sLRb7-OuHag;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
After publishing the newest extensive look at StarRupture co-op gameplay video, we have received a ton of feedback and comments! Thank you for being so active, this helps us understand what you’re most excited about in the game and lets us answer at least some of your questions in this Developer Update. [/p][p]  

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img]
[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/3ab97063cc086577d2c4a96940a5657c74380431.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/eed1507c00b231eadead136283747dbb38338fcc.gif"][/img][/p][p]
The event of the Ruptura’s Fire Wave brings a lot of danger for every living being on the Arcadia-7 planet. But you know what they say - “better safe than sorry”. And that’s where Base Core comes into play. 


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/b0e3d341a2cdfd5547aad6a6fed4fee2baf78cbf.gif"][/img][/p][p]
The passage of the wave of fire does not mean that our base will be wiped out - thanks to the brilliant invention of the Selenian Corp -  Base Cores. Base Cores - crucial for setting up your base - protect and cool down the buildings within their perimeter.  [/p][p]You will also be able to level up the Base Cores so they will be able to restore the factory operations even faster… but it will come at a price, and we’re not necessarily only speaking here about the resources needed to do it…
[/p][previewyoutube="SX5A063JKb4;full"][/previewyoutube][previewyoutube="rQ3ctvERoBE;full"][/previewyoutube][previewyoutube="UifkRFNJkIY;full"][/previewyoutube][p] 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img][/p][p] 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/967517a710c4bb314e78d24c900bfa70c00b0903.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/8c1912809bfdca49716ad19001e1ca84ba890b4d.png"][/img][/p][p]In StarRupture, you and your friends will be able to not only scratch the itch of creating your own, custom factories but also cool and chilling-looking habitats. 

The Habitats you will build across the planet’s surface will be your safe spots. They’re not only perfect hideouts to stock & refill your supplies and plan your next actions, but also great places to hide from the scorching heat or waves of enemies.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/95b46d77e711101449f211f00c801a02edecda01.png"][/img][/p][p]With the building tool, you will be able to create your habitats on the flat lands of the planet, or even more wicked designs on the hill sides. 

You will be able to customize your habitats with additional segments and combine them with vertical or horizontal connectors, add additional airlocks for entrances, and viewports for an extra look at the vistas. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/57c5378a8ff0ad68eaa8d4b52381fe0a45beddda.png"][/img][/p][p]You will also be able to freely decide where to place your storage, progression, and crafting machines. Hopefully, your vision will align with that of your teammates, but if it doesn’t, you can always build another habitat in a different location.[/p][p]We can’t wait to see the creative designs of your habitats you will make in StarRupture. [/p][p]  

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img][/p][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/ad7f14bf4623df3b35594a618d6c0e27d620a2b7.png"][/img][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/8799cb0ae1469f158851b2cd70df002cc5017b9a.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/ad5f34b0171b157f274db8eb8d547413d6c2524e.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/d45feac2126553f6a67082f9e55196e9848d464e.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/5fc09f12c320ab912935c32303190a62ff26b1f6.png"][/img][/carousel][p]In StarRupture, you will be able to take your 3 friends on a mission in which you will extract, automate, and ship the resources from the Arcadia-7 planet.  [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/340575dc680100ca280480b8ded5ccbd01151058.png"][/img][/p][p]You will mark a new chapter in the history of humanity - and the future of the Claywood Corporation - the company that sent you across the galaxy to explore and document this undiscovered world.   [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/8adb55d042144c16fc5228a3f96f980545f77ed1.png"][/img][/p][p]As you progress further, you will uncover different resources that need different machinery to collect them. They have one thing in common, though - Drone Rails. They will not only function as a transportation route to connect them with other machinery or storage buildings, but also as a means to transfer the energy needed to power them.    [/p][p] 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img][/p][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/63b55d5ed3eaa8e898051f9e40c292c35e2791a5.png"][/img][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/fb0521fafd8da4e52b5c6fc71fb00fc6f50a7323.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/dceb1bdf3f33288626ef4a72eab2b07fb3d0cd76.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/585d37ae0b50f0e0540839b685129889e4cad26e.png"][/img][/carousel][p]Last month, we showed you the monoliths - now… we’d like to show you how they’ve changed! [/p][p]They’re now much harder to find - that’s for sure! And they are very much connected to the base defense… but we will reveal more about it later on.  

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/2b2bc035f681f9d471f07b3a59e202bf792fdeb8.png"][/img]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04a2e9a8097ef61ae8ddf26612655282f3309231.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]And that’s all for our StarRupture Developer Update in June - we hope you’ve enjoyed the never-before-seen content and that you’re hungry for more! [/p][p]Stay tuned for our fresh & exciting updates on socials and right here on Steam as well, as we’re on our road to the Autumn 2025 Early Access launch.  [/p][p][/p][p]Until next time,  
[i]Creepy Jar Team[/i]  [/p][p][/p]

Hello Adventurers,

Yes! Now you can paint all kinds of constructions & the newly added decorations. 

After you equip yourself with Paints made from different bugs and other colorful elements, you can create your Paintbrush out of some Fiber, Rope, and a Stick. That is how you can paint your base and color your furniture! Just pick a tint from our Amazonian color collection: white, blue, red, green, or yellow, and make the jungle even more vibrant! 

This mechanic will work with the newly added decorations and the items that you’ve already constructed as well! So be creative, and let your imagination go wild!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/ed9025f71f8580311d0e5a153d991d58c4fdc0ac.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/cd02120adf9c313808cd89e8ffce00962fe152aa.jpg[/img]

You can craft a Table, a Chair, a Bench, a Night Stand and various Paintings to set a proper mood, or even mount some Animal Trophies to show off your hunting skills to others! 

As something extra, we’ve also prepared some Rope, Leaf, and Bone Decorations for those who like pretty (or creepy!) stuff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/698d88c45a5306f26bdcedddc80c44f36efe10ae.jpg[/img]

Just remember - the torches won’t be burning forever and you will need to maintain them if you don’t want to be suddenly surrounded by the darkness of the night again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/e0dbff8c9c28b1fb18628a619e7728ee91e3e0b1.gif[/img]

notes.title: StarRupture Gameplay Reveal!
notes.notes:
Hi, everyone!

We’re very proud to show you for the very first time real gameplay from our upcoming FPP base-builder StarRupture!

In the trailer, you’re gonna see an early glimpse of some of the combat and defense mechanics. You will also see the scale of some of the dangers you will encounter in StarRupture - such as the deadly waves of monster enemies, and most importantly - the Ruptura Star explosion, which scorches the planet’s land with a deadly wave of fire and a blast of (maybe quite important?) meteorites. 

[b]Jump into action in the teaser below: [/b]
[previewyoutube=cbe5Iu7DJVs;full][/previewyoutube][i]Everything you see in the video was live-captured from an early build on PC.[/i]

StarRupture has three main gameplay pillars—[b]base-building[/b], [b]exploration[/b], and [b]combat[/b]—and this action-packed trailer, taken from an early build, gives you a look at the pulse-pounding combat you’ll face in their bid for survival. 

Set in the far future, humanity has gone to the stars in search for precious resources. And the planet orbiting our namesake star, Ruptura, while being a resource-rich open world is also rife with dangers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/9b67fcd6c4f28204296ca6cad9841bfa8d4914a3.jpg[/img]
In the teaser clip, you see our lone explorer face off against hordes of enemies charging a custom-built base. If that isn’t enough, our exploding star is mere minutes from releasing an apocalyptic fire wave on the planet’s surface. 

All of our fighter’s vitals are looking good, but we're not forgetting our roots in survival and eagle-eyed viewers will notice not only the health and armour stats for our player/character, but also the thirst, toxicity, and hunger levels, as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/04d0c536955ca35f04359de687a64813f552dda9.jpg[/img]
Utilizing collected resources to create ammunition to load turrets as one line of defense, the player is valiantly attempting to protect a base under a full-scale assault and there’s no time to waste.

As enemies make their way to destroy the base’s wind farm and storage buildings, a split-second decision is made to protect smelters and crafting pods from a terrifying new enemy assault on the other side of the base. 

While automated drones are busy zipping around their elevated tracks to deliver resources from location to location, the enemy assault becomes all but overwhelming. 
Making matters worse, our soldier looks up to see Ruptura ready to unleash its fiery blaze. With no time left to lose, the race is on to get to safety… but will he make it in time?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/0d50a12105cd0afa3901c20cecc552657866f40d.jpg[/img]
StarRupture sets itself in the story of man versus nature taking place in an otherworldly and breathtaking sci-fi environment where elemental cataclysms of extreme temperatures loom as a constant danger. 

The player takes up the mantle of a convict exiled from the Earth to serve their sentence by mining and expanding industrial production alongside researching new technology on a seemingly hospitable new planet rife with mystery and danger. Tasked with surviving the deadly waves of elements—not to mention facing down against hostile enemy monsters in tense combat—each cycle spells destruction yet ushers in a new era of growth and rebuilding. 

Played from a first-person perspective—adventuring solo or as part of an up-to-4-player group in co-op mode—players will be able to explore, adapt, mine, gather resources, and build complex machinery to survive and prosper.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/55d5dc477a493b2a35e28bac173a12b1c09d9c4e.jpg[/img]
Though by definition it is a base-building simulator, StarRupture is much more. The game will invite players to push beyond, to stay resilient and sharp against every assault, building and forming prior to the cycling eviscerating conditions on an otherwise beautiful planet. 

For fans of builders, management, sci-fi action, and combat StarRupture will challenge all comers to utilize the technology at their fingertips and weather both the extremities and fierce enemies in order to survive and create a prosperous industrial complex. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238153/517a9d4635d16ffc1e85e268cd5424f05c2f5d4a.jpg[/img]

How do you like our first capture of gameplay? We’d love to read your thoughts about it down in the comments section or on our [url=https://discord.gg/starrupture]official Discord channel[/url]. 

Wishlist and follow our game here on Steam and your favorite social media, to be the first to know about our future news for StarRupture.

notes.title: Free Update #20 - Anteater | Available Now!
notes.notes:
Hello Adventurers,

Today is the day! We are proud to announce that the Free Update #20 for Green Hell - "Anteater" is available now! 

The name of our latest free update hides many more new & fresh features than the name might suggest. Alongside having added new animals to your Animal Pen, we’ve prepared a bunch of cool mechanics and enhancements to the rest of the game. See the Anteater in action in the newest trailer, and if you’d like to dive into the update’s details - see the notes below.

[previewyoutube=XZ7FggBdlmU;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/185d57bd83b3e7c3ad142d9c4f8bc96df62955f5.png[/img]

[h2]New animal: [b]Giant Anteater[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/f6c34cab534f56947e13c41fd4bb7264cbbebcb2.gif[/img]
The most exciting part of this update is the Giant Anteater. Some call him amusing, some think he’s cute, but he can be very aggressive - so you need to watch out! 
Naturally, you will be able to find this beast near anthills. He’s usually shy and will try to avoid you, but when threatened - he will not hesitate to use his claws to protect himself and might deal you great damage.


[h2]New mechanic: [b]Spawning anthills[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/59b912c6adcb335d70099d98ff1c9f70917df2dd.jpg[/img]
You may remember anthills from Green Hell before, stepping inside them and getting those pesky ants crawling all over you, or collecting the ants to mend your laceration wounds. But now, anthills may also serve as your guidepost to the place anteaters hang out most.

Until now, the only thing you could have done is either avoid or harvest an anthill. But now you can also destroy them! Destroying an anthill won’t provide you with more ants, but if you find an anthill standing in your way to build something, or if it blocks your path and you keep bumping into it, you will be able to remove it. Don’t worry, though; ants will always find a new spot to build a new house for their colony, so from now on a new anthill will soon appear in a nearby area. With some more animals looking for them, including the infamous anteater and… an armadillo?!


[h2]New mechanic: [b]New animals in your animal pen[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/ab5ca4912f408b0993e0004e46ccd90da78445ce.jpg[/img]
The Animal Husbandry update introduced the ability to breed some of the animal species from the jungle. Now, we are adding even more animals to your menagerie, as you will be able to breed Armadillos, Three-banded Armadillos, and - of course - Giant Anteaters!


[h2]New construction: [b]Composter[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/91bd6769a085586b9dfec90af0a10716ef341911.png[/img]
Thanks to this simple construction you will be able to dispose of such things as rotten meat, spoiled food, leaves, animal drops, and everything organic in general - and not necessarily only expired things! As a product of such action, you will receive compost (see more details about this new item in the section below), and insects with which you will be able to feed your pack of Armadillos and Anteaters.


[h2]New item: [b]Compost[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/90a4a0931b03dc39b6fcaa90a9a6bc5a73de8654.gif[/img]
Show your plants some love with the new, organic, homemade superfood - Compost!
Compost is the most important and most fertilizing product of the Composter. With this nutritious and rich substance, you can elevate your planting skills to a higher level! 


[h2]New construction: [b]Feeding Trough - Insects[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/21d2669ab5b017b730e96cbb8d852295172072b9.png[/img]
As you now have some new pals to take care of in your animal pen, you will need a way to feed them. By using this new construction, you will be able to feed anteaters and armadillos with insects. [i]Bon appétit![/i]


[h2]New mechanic: [b]Parrot keeping[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/998b018fa21f4abedf35ea583f497a03a5ed32a8.gif[/img]
Now you can lure parrots into your base - or any other place where you build a Parrot Nest - where parrots can fly into and become accustomed to your presence.


[h2]New construction: [b]Parrot Nest[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/04cd231222eccc459ac9c4d662e9fa9c269e8627.png[/img]
When you manage to get parrots safe and comfy in your Parrot Nest, you will be rewarded with feathers and eggs left by the birds. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/9f3e1f5311e2b75c3d3d52f56f53517d4e247681.png[/img]
And that’s all in this #20 free content update! As usual, thank you so much for supporting the game. We welcome all your thoughts and feedback on our discord server.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/1916f8b037064d73130a67e42694c1d352bdb51d.gif[/img]
Last but not least, keep your eyes peeled for our next update for Green Hell! Be sure it will make your Amazonian home super cozy!

Happy anteating!

notes.title: Storage & Transportation Update is out now!
notes.notes:
[h1]Dear Adventurers![/h1]
[b]The Storage & Transportation Update[/b] is officially live and available for free for all Steam players! 

[previewyoutube=ooscPx_31EQ;full][Trailer]
[/previewyoutube]

As many of Green Hell’s most experienced players know, efficiency is of the utmost importance if you want to survive in the Amazon jungle. To stay efficient, your base needs perfect space management which improves the process of gathering the necessary food supplies or materials. In addition, every trip across the rainforest puts you in untold danger, so why make more trips than is needed? 

Storage and Transportation patch will help you with that, so just check out what's new:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/185d57bd83b3e7c3ad142d9c4f8bc96df62955f5.png[/img]

[h2]Sled[/h2]
A great tool for transporting heavy objects. What’s more, you can put up to two different types of Heavy Objects in one Sled.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/b04b9e475fdcdbc2b2578381ff586107cde82f53.gif[/img]

[i]We know how much players like to build vast and complex bases. Resources near the base may quickly run out and you have to go deeper and deeper into the jungle for materials. We decided to speed up material transport by adding sleds, to help our players spend more time building and less time running around for materials. [/i]

[h2]Elevator[/h2] 
Treehouse or multi-story villa, the elevator is the new easier way of transporting heavy resources up and down. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/f218293c672127b9e14a9d2dad7b064c4d9ec98d.gif[/img]

[i]In the last building update, we added new construction to build a treehouse. We noticed that transporting a large amount of materials to the upper floors using a ladder is inconvenient, so we decided to add a new construction - an elevator.[/i]

[h2]Shelf and Hanging Shelf[/h2]
A new type of universal storage, in which you can unpack most of the items from your Backpack - excluding weapons and building materials such as sticks (they still need to be put on dedicated stands). Thanks to the new shelves, you can see the status of your stock at a glance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/8f7d90aafe2c6f1e811f70868c765130f3f4369b.png[/img]

[i]We felt that there should be a universal storage for smaller items in Green Hell, where you can see what items it contains without interaction and from a distance. This type of shelf is also aesthetic and looks nice in the base.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/c0afb173cc6c0e47b302f47784c5078f459e1ba1.png[/img]

[h2]Quick Pick Up[/h2]
With the option to turn off animation delay for picking up items you no longer have to wait for animation to complete to pick another item. The faster you click, the faster you pick.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/5be64d6b22bdc0e295cf1dd9268f21253abc1049.gif[/img]

[i]After adding the elevator and sled, we noticed that the delay in the pick-up animation was disrupting the dynamics of the resource harvesting process. That's why we decided to remove this delay. However, during our beta testing, we received feedback that this change affects immersion for some players, so we decided to add the option to disable this improvement in the game options.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/400b72c742444b8f2a3b7e1e06368a2c9bafa2e4.png[/img]

[h2]Baskets[/h2]
A reworked version of the Small and Big Stone Stands are renamed to Baskets and now can hold various types of objects, such as stones, bones, planks, green coconuts, and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/f6f91791dac59990efa0e04cbf467afc432c5ca8.jpg[/img]
[i]As we aim for immersion we thought that the stone basket looks like it can hold similar items, so instead of making new types, we decided to make our stone stands more versatile. Now you can choose what to use it for.[/i]

[h2]New Bamboo versions of Stands[/h2]
Every storage construction now has its bamboo version. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/62d5494f117ba9661b1dee968255fe6c603f1b53.png[/img]

[i]Since The Building Update, we have been trying to give players the opportunity to build their base using any materials. We noticed some wooden structures did not have their bamboo counterparts at all. So, while working on Storage and Transportation Update we wanted to improve the storage system as well by adding a missing bamboo stands.[/i]


[h2]One universal Leaf Stand [/h2]
Leaf Stand now has two slots. You can choose what materials you want to stack in each slot: Banana or Palm leaves. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/6ebdf0d7e2b159836e3f05f629f0f0cd58e74852.png[/img]

[h2]Universal  Wood Stands[/h2]
Stands for logs and sticks made of bamboo or wood can store both wood and bamboo materials in each, e.g. wooden materials can be stored in bamboo racks.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/0aff429d91b2008e1d522c076c69e8d550836a06.png[/img]

[i]So far, the rack system has been very restrictive. For example, to store a Bamboo Log, the player had to build a rack using the same material. It wasn't exactly the optimal solution. So we decided to give players a little more freedom and the ability to change the type of stored material when the structure is already built.[/i]

[h2]Increased capacity of Stands [/h2]
All stands have now increased capacity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/d1668840c8053157d157faf18e8651ea5b10ef31.png[/img]
[i]Since The Building Update, we've been trying to encourage players to build bigger and bigger bases. After playtests, it turned out that the current capacity of material storage structures is simply too small and players have to devote more and more space for these structures.[/i]

[h2]Improved item storing & pick-up mechanic[/h2]
Now you can place and take out an item in storage with a single button, and take it out with another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/bcc715f2a8c1a31ae6049075ae16c326edb64f07.png[/img]

[list]
[*]	Game no longer crashes after trying to stack Armadillo Meat together with other meats
[*]	System of construction snapping was reworked. It is now more convinient to attach Ghosts to already built Constructions
[*]	Snapping the Ladder to Triangular Frames is adjusted
[*]	Building and using Climbing Places is now more convinient
[*]	Improved render distance of constructions added in Building Update
[*]	Tree Platforms' Ghosts now collide with each other, preventing from building new inside the existing one
[*]	Player can no longer snap multiple Construction Ghosts to one spot
[*]	Frog Stretcher progress icon now updates properly for all Players in co-op session
[*]	Already placed construction Ghost doesn't disappear when player rapidly presses Q just after placing it
[*]	Mud Fireside Wall can be now properly built on Tringular Frames with roof on top
[*]	Triangular Banana Leaf Roof now properly casts shadow
[*]	Size of Notebook Constructions drawings is adjusted
[*]	Doors now have proper state after reloading the save
[*]	Disabling Head Bob no longer causes input issues when fighting with the Tribes
[*]	Players' input should no longer be blocked when petting an animal in crowded environment
[*]	Opening Notebook / Map during Blowgun reload animation no longer causes an input lock
[*]	Pressing a right stick on a Controller no longer causes crafting animation to loop
[*]	Player longer gets stuck when opening Map / Notebook while using the Pottery Table
[*]	Sample Analyzer in Story can be now properly used by any Player in co-op session after the reload
[*]	Ghost for putting down Kid in Spirits of Amazonia villages is now properly displayed for all players in co-op session
[*]	Player is no longer able to craft Spirits of Amazonia arena weapons during the Tutorial
[*]	Kid from the Spirits of Amazonia first village no longer falls down the bridge after being spawned
[*]	It should no longer be possible to bypass the Snake Pass in Spirits of Amazonia
[*]	Picking up the Kid from the deep water now works properly
[*]	Planting Boxes put on the Triantular Frames' roofs now get proper hydration from the rain
[*]	Changing name of a fruit directly on a plant now works properly
[*]	Climbing on Floating Frames while carrying multiple Heavy Objects now works properly
[*]	Player can now put only one Heavy Object of each type on the Crafting Table
[*]	Heavy objects are no longer stuck to Player's hands while drowning
[*]	Stingray Sting can be now used to remove underskin worm
[*]	Unlocking Animal Pen by interacting with Snare Trap now gives a proper notification
[*]	Player can no longer tranqulize baby animals
[*]	Gender of the animal no longer changes randomly when reloading a session
[*]	After session reload, animals no longer disappear if they were called
[*]	Name of the tied animal no longer resets to default after session reload
[*]	Unlit fire no longer displays overlapping text
[*]	Unlit Torch no longer displays overlapping text when trying to ignite it from Campfire
[*]	All small items can now be properly picked up from the slots at the Campfire
[*]	"Items that are put on the campfire by using 'insert' button should be fully visible"
[*]	Player can no longer place soups or infusions in Clay Bottle
[*]	Big Stone no longer disapperas from the Crafting Table after running while using Controller
[*]	Bowls thrown into deep water can now be properly picked up
[*]	Trunks of cut down large palms now work properly after a session reload
[*]	Players are now able to wash themselves in any body of water while standing under cover
[*]	Fishes cought by spear fishing now always land in Inventory of Player who cought it in co-op session
[*]	Two hand axes now take one hit to destroy Green Coconut
[*]	Resetting Key Bindings to default now works properly
[*]	Player can now save changes on the frame rate error pop-up
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/18cf59525a9f8a6b0ae5430045a5f281830acf58.jpg[/img]

We hope that you liked all the updates and they will definitely improve the comfort of “living” in the Amazon jungle. All these new improvements will allow you to fully devote yourself to the adventure, as well as build your dream house and spend more time petting capybaras.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/92c3c845cf8dd4a62b79d49ff5d1f9a174da1f9a.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/18f8ae29663b7efa43f458dc789158f1f888f674.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/185d57bd83b3e7c3ad142d9c4f8bc96df62955f5.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev Notes
notes.notes:
[b]Adventurers![/b]

For this Developer Notes, I'd like to share some information about [b]cooperation mode[/b] and [b]Nvidia GeForce NOW.[/b]

[u][b]
COOP MODE![/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/f0aed0fd4d240816d85f5e35b5f296b1ed604799.jpg[/img]

Our work on Cooperative mode continues at a steady pace. Our in game Cooperative Jake testers are playing daily, updating the development team about balance, bugs, crashes and (of course) the fun factor.

Green Hell cooperative mode will have no in game voice capabilities but will employ in game text chat. The Official Green Hell discord will implement an array of voice lobbies for gamers to utilize when cooperative mode is live, so keep an eye out for Sifner to bring up those channels (and the associated rules) in the future.

Cooperative mode will be handled in both 'public' and 'private' game lobbies.

[b][u]GEFORCE NOW[/u][/b]

GeForce NOW is a streaming service from NVIDIA, which is a similar service to Google Stadia, Microsoft xCloud or PlayStation Now.

Last week GeForce Now ended their beta phase, making it available to all interested parties (including here in Poland!)

Using GeForce Now players can launch selected games from their Steam collection on any PC, Mac, TV or Android phone. You won't have to worry about performance as the image is streamed directly from the NVIDIA cloud. You don't even have to re-buy a game you already own - GeForce NOW connects to the Valve platform and will utilize that library directly.

Because it's still in it's early days, GeForce Now does not work with all Steam games currently.

However.

NVIDIA has chosen an array of interesting games to be amongst the first cloud based offerings and we are pleased to announce that [u][b]Green Hell [/b][/u]has been chosen to be amongst this list of starting titles, making it one of the first Polish games to be offered on the service.

Green Hell within GeForce Now will allow you to survive the dangerous Amazon jungle even on a non-gaming laptop. Details of the free GeForce Now package, as well as information about the optional subscription, are available here : https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/

notes.title: Jungle survival sim Green Hell now has multi-story mud huts, co-op soon
notes.notes:
Green Hell, the amazonian survival game that made Christopher Livingston so mad he punched an armadillo, now has mud huts with two, even three stories. Remarkable, I know. The Expanded Shelters update brings the ability to make your mud and bamboo buildings into multi-story wonders with new doors, walls, ladders and ceilings. Just imagine the possibilities: A sprawling mud mansion, a clay castle, a veritable Versailles of molded muck, a manor in the mire, perhaps even several châteaux of sprawling, stately sludge.

A survival crafting game highlighting the challenges of jungle environments, Green Hell released earlier this year and ranks as one of Steam’s Best of 2019 new releases, according to Valve. It’s one of those few survival games with a full single player campaign, like The Forest. Expanded Shelters is the second content update to the game since its full release, following last month’s plant cultivation expansion. The next update is slated to add a cooperative mode to Green Hell, according to the developers’ roadmap, and should release in early 2020.

You can find Green Hell on Steam, presently 20% in the winter sale, or go check out the official website.

Today, as I neared the summit of moss-slicked ridge on the outskirts of a fuggy mangrove swamp, I encountered what can only be described as a discovery that will shake the very foundations of ornithology.

A flock of brilliantly coloured birds, flying in a such a way as to spell out: Green Hell is a first person survival game set in the Amazon rainforest. You play amnesiac American anthropologist Jake Higgins, as he attempts to brave nature, build shelters, hunt and fight, find his missing wife, and avoid eating so many poisonous mushrooms that he craps himself to death. Truly, we are but mewling babes in the face of nature s many undiscovered permutations.

notes.title: Green Hell Launches into 1.0
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32791864/82743b2db6a63bd31e9c7577ac1c6f3d74725e08.jpg[/img]

[h1]We are excited to announce that Green Hell leaves Early Access and launches into 1.0. ![/h1]

[u]Watch the Green Hell 1.0 Lauch Trailer:[/u]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOCzDVTsfug

Green Hell saw huge improvements and regular updates during the Early Access phase and now sees a ton of new features accompany this momentous launch. 
From an entirely new map area to new animals and custom difficulty settings, the 1.0 update is Green Hell’s largest yet. Story Mode, one of the most anticipated features of all, will see players test more than just their survival skills as they embark on a desperate mission to navigate the deadly Amazon rainforest and rescue their lost love, Mia.

In the year since Green Hell launched into Early Access, we have worked continuously on improving the game alongside incorporating feedback from our dedicated
community. See the list of additions and changes below:

[h1]Story Mode and 1.0 Update Additions[/h1]
● Story Mode! — How did you end up in the Amazon? What happened to your love, Mia?
How can you escape? How can you survive? Seeking answers to these questions will
take you to the brink of sanity as you rediscover well-known areas and discover new
areas for the first time.
● New Map Areas — The lush rainforest of Green Hell gets even bigger with new
Wetlands to explore. Also included, is an all-new in-game map!
● Perma-Death Difficulty — Gear up for the most ruthless challenge yet. There’s no
coming back from death.
● New Graphics Options — Optimize your experience with new FOV, Vsync, antialiasing,
texture quality, and shadow distance options.
● New Plants and Animals — Introducing the psychosis-inducing Psychotria Viridis, the
Banisterposis Caapi, and the lethally poisonous Dart Frog.
● Decay Timer— Many items in the game will now start to wither and decay. Players will
have to be vigilant learning to use their items before they expire.
● New Difficulty Levels (Tourist, King of the Jungle, Custom) — Have a problem with
snakes? Maybe spiders? Introducing new difficulty options to turn tribes, predators,
spiders, snakes, and the sanity meter on or off! Hate managing macroelements? Green
Hell is also adding a depletion speed slider to adjust how quickly you need to replenish
yourself.

notes.title: Green Hell, the survival sim set in the Amazon, leaves Early Access soon
notes.notes:
Green Hell, the intense survival simulator set in the Amazon jungle, will launch out of  Early Access on September 5. The game's been in Early Access for nearly a year, and currently boasts a 'Very Positive' rating on Steam. Chris played it in October, and became so enraged that he punched an armadillo (in the game, not in real life). Becoming enraged is, of course, par for the course in survival games, so it bodes well.

The game has rapidly expanded since its August 2018 Early Access release: the map has swollen and new animals and enemies have been added, among other things. As for what will be added come September 5, there's quite a bit, including a new Wetlands area of the map, a perma-death difficulty, new plants and animals, and a 'Decay Timer', which sounds great.

As for the story mode, this is all we know thus far: "How did you end up in the Amazon? What happened to your love, Mia? How can you escape? How can you survive? Seeking answers to these questions will take you to the brink of sanity as you rediscover well-known areas and discover new areas for the first time."

Here's a new trailer:

notes.title: Green Hell Release Date Announcement
notes.notes:
Creepy Jar is excited to announce that Green Hell will be leaving Early Acces and launching 1.0 at: [b]Sept 5, 2019[/b]

Releasing into Early Access in August of 2018, Green Hell comes full circle just over one year later as it launches into version 1.0. 

Continuing our focus on listening to the Green Hell community, Creepy Jar has also implemented a number of changes and fixes to coincide with the 1.0 launch update. See a list of the major additions in the update below;

[h1]Story Mode and 1.0 Update Additions:[/h1]

●	[b]Story Mode![/b] — How did you end up in the Amazon? What happened to your love, Mia? How can you escape? How can you survive? Seeking answers to these questions will take you to the brink of sanity as you rediscover well known areas and discover new areas for the first time.
●	[b]New Map Areas[/b] — The lush rainforest of Green Hell gets even bigger with new Wetlands to explore.
●	[b]Perma-Death Difficulty[/b] — Gear up for the most ruthless challenge yet. There’s no coming back from death.
●	[b]New Graphics Options[/b] — Optimize your experience with new FOV, Vsync, antialiasing, texture quality, and shadow distance options.
●	[b]New Plants and Animals[/b] — Introducing the psychosis-inducing Psychotria Viridis, the banisteriopsis Caapi, and the lethally poisonous Dart Frog.
●	[b]Decay Timer[/b]— Many items in the game will now start to wither and decay. Players will have to be vigilant learning to use their items before they expire.
●	[b]Custom Game Settings[/b] – Have a problem with snakes? Maybe spiders? Introducing new options to turn tribes, predators, spiders, snakes, and the sanity meter on or off! notes.title: Green Hell 1.0 Delayed to Summer 2019
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, 

We want to start off by thanking you all for your support, Green Hell would not be what it is without all of your input.

In the interest of transparency, we want you all to know that we need some extra time to bring the full release of Green Hell to you.

We have decided to move from Unity 2017 to Unity 2018 (the engine used to make the game), in order to bring a better looking and more optimized experience. This will also help us realize the full potential of the story mode, add a massive map expansion, new enemies, implement your feedback and more.

Our new release date is for Summer 2019, and in the meantime, we will have the Mud Update which will arrive within the next few weeks! Featuring new items and crafting alongside the addition of mud-based buildings and apparatus.

We look forward to continuing this journey with you!

notes.title: Survival game Green Hell made me so mad I pummeled an innocent armadillo
notes.notes:
I've only been in the Amazon for about eleven seconds and I've already got a rash. I spawned in the jungle, looked around, took two steps forward, brushed up against a bush, and wound up immediately covered with tiny spiders. As a result, my arm has broken out in an unpleasant rash, which oddly enough, makes me immensely happy. I've never had a rash in a game before! I love when a game gives me a completely new experience, even if it's an unpleasant one.

It also gives me a goal I've never had before (in a game, at least): cure my rash! That turns out to be extremely difficult, because hours later I've been killed a dozen times from falls, wounds, venom, arrows, disease, and dehydration, and I eventually get so frustrated I find myself squatting in the dirt and pummeling an innocent armadillo with my bare fists out of sheer frustration.

This is Green Hell, an Early Access first-person survival game that feels a lot like The Forest only it's set in the rain forests of the Amazon. The tutorial gives you the basics of crafting, health, and keeping your bearings, as well as explaining why you're lost in the Amazon with a high-tech watch but no matches or food. And a rash.

I like a lot of things about Green Hell immediately. You've got a cool wristwatch that acts as a compass and a status indicator, displaying your health and hydration. The crafting system is entirely sensible in that one stick + one rock = one stone axe. To make a spear you need a stick, a sharp rock, and a vine. Are you paying attention, other survival games that require more than one stick and more than one rock to make a stone axe? Green Hell has put you on notice.

I also like how you have to inspect your body to see what affliction(s) you've got by actually looking at your limbs and moving them around with the mouse. My spider rash, for example, shows up as inflamed bumps on my arm. Walk through a puddle and you might pick up a few leeches, which you can pluck off and drop with your mouse while staring down at your legs in horror. If a worm burrows under your skin while you sleep, and they will, you can—wait, I'm getting ahead of myself.

The first step in Green Hell, unfortunately, is not to cure my rash but to build a shelter. I say unfortunately because having a shelter is the only way you can save your game. I'm not a fan of games that don't just let you save whenever you want, and I'm especially not a fan of getting killed by a leopard while I'm trying to build a shelter so I can save my game, which is exactly what happens. I've crafted an axe, chopped down some trees, gathered some sticks, and I'm just putting on the finishing touches (placing a lot of palm leaves on top) when a leopard runs up and claws me to death.

This is a double setback, because not only do I have to start over from square one and rebuild my nearly-built shelter, but I also need to reacquire my rash so I can then cure my rash. I re-craft and re-gather and re-build, and finally manage to save my game, and then I go off blundering into the bushes hoping to wind up covered in spiders.

Somehow I can't re-contract my rash, though plenty of other horrible things happen. I'm attacked by a leopard again, and while I chase him away with a few blows of my axe, he's lacerated my calves and I can't craft a bandage quickly enough to stop bleeding. I die. While tromping around on my next life I'm bitten by a snake, poisoned, contract a fever, and die while trying to sleep it off. Well, technically, I sleep, wake up, stand up, and then die. While trying to jump a gap in a bridge, I plummet and fall to my demise. I run into some natives, they make quick work of me with a few arrows and melee weapons.

Green Hell, in other words, is pretty brutal, just as it should be given its setting. And mostly, it's the damn leopard. He always seems to find me within a minute of reloading a save, so I decide to start completely over. This guide to Green Hell gives compass coordinates to the safest area of the map, so I start a new game, spawn, and start running toward the safe(r) zone. How many times do I die along the way? I'd say about seven. Leopards. Snakes. Another fall off a log bridge. Natives. One time, I get so close I die within sight of the valley I'm heading for. And I can't save without building a shelter, so I have to start from scratch every damn time.

Finally, I make it. I build my shelter, save my game, and set out once more to get a rash. I don't get a rash, and I don't get killed by leopards, but I'm bitten by a snake. After trying to sleep off the fever, I'm parched, so foolishly I drink from the river, which gives me a worse fever. I've also got worms burrowing under my skin, which I removed with a needle I've crafted from the bones of a fish I killed with my spear (which was pretty cool, really), but I need a bandage for the sore, and while I'm out looking for the one damn kind of plant I can make a bandage from, I'm bitten by another snake. I'm so annoyed I kill it with my spear and devour it raw and get parasites. I'm a mess.

There are plenty of bright spots along the way. I learn to set out coconut shells near my camp to catch rain water for drinking. I can make a fire and cook meat. And the Amazon of Green Hell is quite lovely, especially in the valley. Bad things only ever happen when I stop looking at it and take a few steps in any direction.

I finally do contract my rash again! It's on my leg this time, because both of my arms already have wounds from worms that have burrowed into my skin and have been removed with fishbones. Happy and relieved to be back on track, I walk off to seek a cure for my long sought-after rash and I'm immediately bitten again by a snake. Dammit! Now I'm gonna die of snakes before I can cure the rash it took me two hours to find!

I hate the Amazon. I hate it. All I want is to get a rash and cure it, and all it wants is for me to get everything else and die. An armadillo skitters by and I pounce on him, pummeling furiously him with both fists until I'm completely out of stamina. Don't worry, the armadillo is fine. I'm the only wounded one, here, and I'll die of any number of ailments long before I've gotten rid of this beautiful, elusive rash.

notes.title: Green Hell Early Access Date Announcement
notes.notes:
We are excited to announce that their first-person, psychological survival simulator, Green Hell will be hitting Steam Early Access on August 29th, 2018! Set in the uncharted depths of the sweltering Amazon rainforest players will be challenged at every turn in a desperate quest for survival. From the harsh rainforest environment to its wild inhabitants, the player may never know friend from foe until it’s too late. Check out the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T_V4RhejHo]all new Green Hell Early Access trailer![/url]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T_V4RhejHo

Upon the Early Access release, players will be able to dive into a full one half of the final map, encounter five dangerous and hostile creatures, and learn how to inspect their bodies for all kinds of wounds, infections, and parasitic nasties. Not only that, they can get a sneak peek into the Story Mode with a fully voiced over tutorial introduction.

Beginning its journey with a huge amount of content, Green Hell players can also look forward to updates containing new tribal enemies, cool new death animations, a water update introducing diving and fishing, and even more languages beyond the initial offerings of English, French, Italian, German and Spanish. Stay tuned for more updates on Green Hell’s development roadmap!


[h1]﻿Key Features[/h1]

[b]Realistic Survival Simulator[/b] - Green Hell puts great focus on realism in both its world building and gameplay. Everything that is crafted or built is necessary for survival, and was consulted on with experts. The Amazon is not a typical forest; threats are literally crawling under your skin.

[b]Psychological Thriller[/b]  - Waking up in the middle of the Amazon with no recollection of how you got there or how you’ll get out, the hardest battle you’ll face is the fight against yourself and your weaknesses and fears.

[b]Fully Alive Amazon Rainforest[/b] - Every effort has gone into recreating the lush world of the Amazon in painstaking detail. An exotic and dangerous place, this jungle is filled with many hazards beyond predators including toxic plants, illnesses and infections, all waiting to bring the player to their demise.

[b]Body Inspection[/b] - Dangers lurk around every bend but they also live under your very skin. Paramount to your survival is checking your body for parasites, infections, and wounds. Take care or suffer the consequences.

---

[i]A big thank you to everyone who has shown their excitement for the game, we look forward to providing you with more updates leading up to the early access launch![/i]
